# Governance

This is an independent civic research blueprint. It is not a House, Senate, prosecutorial or law-enforcement body. The release does not identify anyone as having committed a crime.

Maintainers control scope and releases. Legal editors review authorities and distinguish present law from proposals. Evidence reviewers inspect source support and counterevidence. Privacy/security reviewers assess disclosure and software. A contributor cannot approve the contributor's own packet. Different handles do not prove different people or independent operators; enrollment must verify identities and conflicts through a real administrative process.

The initial connected account is Foundup. Before accepting investigative findings for publication, enroll additional independent reviewers and configure protected main, required actual approvals, code-owner review for legal/executable/publication files, and a main-only deployment environment. Evidence publication is disabled in `data/publication-policy.json` until those prerequisites are met. CODEOWNERS and reviewer strings alone do not establish or enforce this governance.

The trusted approval registry binds exact packet SHA-256 bytes to human review decisions. It must be administratively protected. A graph edge cannot publish merely because an author marks a JSON review field approved. The public-file manifest separately controls method/document downloads; newly added files require explicit review and manifest entry. No public repository is the governmental restricted evidence vault.

Changes to core legal assumptions require an authoritative source, effective-date analysis and an independent reviewer. Security changes require tests proportionate to risk. A release requires legal/editorial approval, a reproducible successful build and a clear description of limitations. Preserve prior releases and a correction ledger; retire affected claims and derivatives when their premise fails.

No maintainer or agent may claim to act for a government office without actual delegated authority. State referrals and institutional correspondence require separate authorization, counsel review, verified recipients and lawful disclosure. The autonomous layer can propose a review task; it cannot make those decisions.
